hero.title: Fixing Science Using a New Science of Science
hero.subtitle: How do we understand and learn about the world? By gathering information. If we perform enough experiments and write down what happens, eventually we should be able to understand how everything works. This approach seems logical, and it is the basis of most science, particularly biology, psychology, and social sciences. It underlies much of the progress of scientific knowledge over the past hundred years. Surprisingly, however, this form of empirical approach turns out to be inherently limited in what it can do.
